imageAlt: Illustrative navy earring gift box and removable display card
title: Earring Card in a Gift Box: Protect Posts and Make Removal Easy
seoTitle: Earring Card Gift Box: Post Clearance and Fit | MTT
summary: Plan the earring card, post clearance and customer removal before approving a presentation box.
intro: A card can make earrings easy to see, but the posts and backs need space behind it. Before approving the box, measure the complete earrings with their fastenings and decide how the customer will remove the card. Check the loaded sample, closed lid and outer shipping pack with the actual jewellery.
cta: Share your product dimensions, artwork, packing location, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review a custom packaging brief from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Measure the complete earring, not only its face

Ask for the largest finished pair, including the post, backing, decorative element and any protective sleeve. Record the post projection behind the display face, the overall width of the pair and the parts that should not touch paper or adhesive. If several earring styles share a card, compare each backing as well as the decorative front.

A post that fits the card hole may still press against the box floor when the card is loaded. Draw the card position and the free space behind it on the section view, then review the actual assembly. A photograph or nominal card size cannot establish that clearance.
Separate card retention from earring retention

Decide how the card is held in the box and how the earrings are fixed to the card. A slot, ledge or folded support may retain the card, but it must also leave a safe path for the posts and backs. Ask the jewellery supplier which surfaces may contact the support and how the piece should be handled.

Illustrative scenario: the same card holds studs with two different backs. The decorative fronts are equal, but one backing projects farther. Approving only the smaller backing may leave insufficient space on the second version. This is an example, not an MTT order or test result.
Make removal and lid clearance observable

Try removing and replacing the card without pulling on either earring. A finger recess or tab may help; make sure the tab does not trap the lid or cover the jewellery. Close the box with the proposed tissue, care card and all fastenings present. Look for contact marks on the card and lid, and record the agreed card orientation.

Compare the necklace chain management guide for a different jewellery-removal problem; necklace slots do not automatically solve stud-post clearance.
Review the complete set and quote

The earring card box is an illustrative design reference. Ask the supplier to quote box, card, optional pouch and bag, samples, tooling and freight as separate items. If the jewellery travels by carrier, discuss the complete outer pack and suitable test scope with the brand and laboratory. ISTA distinguishes product-and-pack testing procedures according to the relevant distribution situation.[1]
What to send MTT

Send the actual earring dimensions and back type, photos, required card orientation, quantity per design, logo artwork and destination. MTT can review a custom packaging brief from 1,000 boxes per design; final structure, colours and branding are confirmed by sample.
Record a useful sample decision

At the sample review, place the loaded card into the box in the agreed orientation. Record the space behind the deepest backing, the tab or recess used for removal and whether the earrings remain seated during ordinary handling. A different backing can change the result even when the visible earring is unchanged.

Earring-card sample record
CheckRecord with the sample
Card retentionSupport type, insertion direction and artwork revision
Post and backActual backing type and clearance observation
RemovalWhere the customer grips and any contact with the jewellery
Closed packAll tissue, card and lid components present during review

Define acceptable marks and movement with the brand; the table is a review framework, not a laboratory test.
Sources
1. ISTA: packaged-product test procedure families, accessed 18 November 2026.

imageAlt: Illustrative six-vial folding paperboard sleeve and tray concept
title: Six-Vial Paperboard Sleeve and Tray: Fit and Pack-Out
seoTitle: Six-Vial Paperboard Sleeve and Tray: Fit Guide | MTT
summary: Design a folding paperboard sleeve, vial tray and card space around the capped samples and packing sequence.
intro: A six-vial discovery set needs more than six equal openings. Measure the capped samples, choose how the tray will be erected and loaded, and check that cards and vials clear the sleeve as it slides. Approve the printed, loaded sample rather than relying on an unassembled dieline.
cta: Share your product dimensions, artwork, packing location, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review a custom packaging brief from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Choose a realistic vial orientation

Record the maximum capped length, body diameter and filled weight for every vial, including labels and seams. Draw the tray with the same orientation the packing team will use. A channel needs to locate the vial while allowing fingers to lift it without pulling the sprayer or cap.

A six-vial set with two cap sizes may need two channel shapes or a tested common support. A repeated graphic opening is not proof that both samples fit. The image illustrates a concept, not measured tolerances or a completed production run.
Plan tray folds and sleeve travel together

The folded tray walls, glue tabs, print and the full card stack all occupy space. Erect the tray using the intended board, then slide it empty into the sleeve. Add the insert, vials and cards one stage at a time and identify where resistance begins. Inspect folding, edge contact and any rubbing at the opening after repeated handling appropriate to the project.

Holmen explains creasing and folding as linked operations in paperboard conversion; the board and crease design should be reviewed as a system rather than assigning a universal crease setting.[1]
Agree the card and version handoff

Measure the complete scent-card stack and decide whether it sits beside or above the vials. Check that it does not protrude into the sleeve opening or press on a cap. Use a position map linking vial, card and artwork version; the scent-identification guide covers that operational control in more detail.
Compare the loaded and empty pack

An empty tray can slide well yet bind once the product or insert changes its shape. Check the loaded sample, safe removal and the intended outer shipping pack. Compare the folding paperboard concept with the four-vial rigid drawer concept; their materials and illustrated contents differ, so sample the chosen specification.
What to include in the brief

Send capped vial samples or supplier drawings, filled weights, set count, card stack dimensions, proposed assembly location, artwork, quantity by design and destination. MTT can review projects from 1,000 pieces per design, with paper, colours, logo and final fit confirmed on a sample.
Compare two packing layouts before tooling

Illustrative example: six vials lie in one row, and a folded leaflet is added beside them. On the first trial, the leaflet catches the sleeve edge. The team can move the leaflet into a shallower pocket or change its fold, then repeat the loading sequence with representative printed parts. This is a planning example, not a completed order.

Ask for the tray blank and sleeve to be reviewed together. Holmen describes crease formation as a material-dependent conversion process; request a physical sample on the proposed board instead of transferring a crease setting from a different substrate. Record which side is printed, where adhesive is applied and whether the assembly is supplied flat or erected. Keep the same vial and card versions when comparing revisions.
Sources
1. Holmen: paperboard creasing and folding, accessed 18 November 2026.

imageAlt: Illustrative cosmetic gift box; scented components require separate supplier verification
title: Scented Cards in Cosmetic Gift Boxes: A Supplier Coordination Brief
seoTitle: Scented Cards in Cosmetic Gift Boxes: Buyer Brief | MTT
summary: Separate scent formulation, card finishing and presentation-box responsibilities before planning a scented insert.
intro: A scented card is a separate component from the structural insert that holds a cosmetic product. Before including it in a gift set, identify who supplies the fragrance and card, who assesses the intended use and who checks contact with packaging. Confirm suitability and any requirements with the relevant suppliers; availability is project-specific.
cta: Share your product dimensions, artwork, packing location, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review a custom packaging brief from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Define the component and responsibility

A buyer might refer to a loose scent strip, a pre-scented card in a sleeve, or a paper insert printed with instructions. These are different components. Record who formulates and applies the fragrance, who provides the paper and who packs the finished card. The packaging illustration is not evidence that MTT supplies scented-card manufacture or fragrance treatment.
Ask the fragrance supplier the right question

Provide the intended finished use, destination markets, fragrance mixture, application method and expected contact with the consumer. Ask the fragrance supplier and responsible product team which documents and assessments apply. IFRA says its certificate concerns a fragrance mixture for a specified intended use and does not replace a safety assessment or applicable law.[1] Do not describe a whole box as “IFRA certified” merely because a document exists for a fragrance mixture.
Review contact and segregation

Agree whether the scented card will touch a product label, pouch, printed finish or another fragrance sample. Ask the relevant suppliers what contact, transfer, staining, odour migration or storage checks they recommend for the actual materials. An unscented control and a representative finished pack help the team identify differences, but any formal test method and acceptance criteria should be agreed by qualified parties.

Illustrative scenario: a loose card is placed directly against an uncoated paper insert. The brand wants the paper surface to remain unmarked. Before approving production, the brand and card supplier agree the contact arrangement, observation period and acceptability criteria. This is not an MTT case or test result.
Keep packing versions identifiable

If one campaign uses several scents, link the fragrance reference, card artwork, sleeve and box version in a pack-out list. Keep a physical approved reference and explain which side faces the product. The discovery-set identification guide offers a related control for matching components.
Ask for an itemised packaging brief

Send card dimensions, whether a separate sleeve is supplied, packing sequence, artwork, intended market, quantity and the responsible scent supplier. MTT can review box and paper-packaging requirements for projects from 1,000 boxes per design. Confirm availability of any scented component and its assessment separately; no blanket scent-service claim is made here.
Separate the approval records

Keep the packaging artwork revision, card material reference, fragrance mixture document and actual packing instruction as separate records. The party responsible for the finished consumer product determines which assessments and market-specific rules apply; a packaging supplier should not replace that assessment with a general claim.

Questions to assign before sampling
ItemQuestion
FragranceWho supplies the mixture and confirms intended use?
CardWho applies, sleeves and labels it?
BoxWhich surfaces can touch the card?
PackingHow are scent and artwork versions identified?

Only the relevant supplier can confirm its own component; availability and charges remain subject to quotation.
Sources
1. IFRA: using the Standards and certificates, accessed 18 November 2026.

imageAlt: Illustrative jewellery box and removable earring card concept
title: Jewellery Box and Earring Card: Align a Custom Logo Before Print
seoTitle: Jewellery Box and Earring Card Logo Approval | MTT
summary: Coordinate artwork, material and proof approval for a jewellery box and its removable display card.
intro: The same logo file can appear different on a textured box wrap and a smooth earring card. Decide which surface carries the main brand mark, share production-ready artwork, and compare finished physical samples. Confirm placement relative to the earrings, card slot and box opening before approving the print run.
cta: Share your product dimensions, artwork, packing location, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review a custom packaging brief from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Start with the viewing sequence

Mark where the customer first sees the box, then where the card appears when the lid opens. A box lid can carry a larger mark while the card may need a smaller mark that remains visible beside the jewellery. Leave practical space for holes, tabs, product and any required retail information; the designer and converter should confirm the actual dieline.
Describe the artwork and finish separately

Provide vector artwork where available, the intended colour, approximate placement and reference sample. Identify whether the box and card use the same print process or different finishes such as ink and foil. Discuss fine lines, paper texture and edge proximity with the converter; a screen rendering cannot establish final registration or legibility.

The blind-deboss guide covers a particular finishing process; this guide deals with the two-component layout and approval.
Check the card with the actual earrings

Load the earring card with the real posts and backs. Check that the product does not obscure the logo, that a hole or tab does not cut into the artwork and that the logo remains upright when the card is seated. Try removal without touching the decorated face unnecessarily. Confirm the depth behind the card separately in the earring clearance guide.
Approve one reference for each surface

Ask for the chosen box wrap and card material in the same proof review. Record the artwork revision, substrate, finish and agreed reference under consistent viewing conditions. If a material or finish changes, check the affected component again. A matching digital colour value alone is not evidence that two different surfaces will look identical.

If a barcode or QR code is required, reserve its quiet zone and check it on the finished print; GS1 notes that contrast, surface and surrounding graphics affect 2D symbol readability.[1]
Request an itemised quotation

Send the box concept, card size, jewellery dimensions, logo artwork, quantity per design and destination. Ask for box, card, print or foil tooling, sample and optional bag costs separately. MTT projects start at 1,000 boxes per design; colours, logos and materials remain customizable.
Compare physical proofs with a shared record

Illustrative example: the same gold artwork is applied to a textured navy box and a smooth ivory card. The team agrees which component is the visual reference, reviews both under the same light and records the approved foil and paper combinations. The process does not promise an identical appearance on different materials.

Mark the earring holes, card edge and any tab on the proof. When the card is seated, a hole position or product can cover a logo that looked centred in a flat file. Keep the physical approval sample and final file revision together; ask how a change in card supplier, finish or artwork will be communicated before reorder.
Sources
1. GS1: 2D barcodes at retail point of sale, accessed 18 November 2026.

imageAlt: Illustrative folding paperboard discovery set; comparison requires matching real product specifications
title: Six-Vial Discovery Sets: Compare Folding Paperboard and Rigid Boxes
seoTitle: Six-Vial Discovery Set: Folding vs Rigid Box | MTT
summary: Compare the complete six-vial pack, assembly and freight scope before selecting a presentation structure.
intro: A folding paperboard sleeve and tray and a rigid drawer can both present sample vials, but the comparison must include the insert, card, assembly and outer shipment. Use the same six capped vials, quantity and destination for both quotations, and review loaded samples before choosing on unit price alone.
cta: Share your product dimensions, artwork, packing location, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review a custom packaging brief from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Make the scope equal

Give each supplier the same six vial dimensions, filled weights, cap types, card stack, artwork and intended distribution route. Specify 1,000 or more boxes per design. Ask whether each quote covers the sleeve or shell, tray or insert, card pocket, print, sample, setup and export packing. A lower box-only figure is not directly comparable to a packed-set quote.
Consider assembly and storage

A paperboard tray may arrive flat and need folding, insertion and vial loading at the packing location. A rigid drawer may arrive assembled, but its insert and cards can still require separate steps. Confirm how each component is delivered and who erects and packs it; do not infer labour time from a render.

Illustrative comparison: if one option requires two additional assembly operations for each of 1,000 sets, record those 2,000 operations in the packing plan and time a representative trial. This arithmetic is not a measured MTT labour result or an estimated cost.
Measure the complete shipment

Ask for the number of cartons, carton dimensions and gross weights for shells, trays and inserts separately. Calculate physical cubic metres for each carton size as outside length × width × height in metres × carton count, then sum the results. A carrier may charge on a different basis, so obtain comparable actual quotations for the same destination and service.
Review each loaded sample

Check sleeve travel, folded corners, insert retention, safe vial removal and card clearance for the paperboard concept. For a rigid drawer, compare the actual tray, pull and cavity layout; the existing four-vial concept shows a different count, so it is a structural reference rather than a like-for-like price comparison.

Discuss the complete outer pack and test requirements with the brand and laboratory. ISTA distinguishes an early screening test from tests designed around distribution environments.[1]
Decide with a common checklist

Record the approved opening, product access, appearance, packing work, carton plan and delivery terms for each option. Confirm material, print, logo, sample charge and schedule on the actual specification. The broader rigid-versus-carton guide explains family differences; this comparison focuses on the same discovery-set brief.
A like-for-like quotation checklist

Keep the comparison on the same scope
Cost or taskQuestion for both suppliers
PackagingAre the tray, insert and card space included?
Set-upAre printing, die and sample charges separated?
AssemblyWho erects the box and loads the vials?
FreightAre destination, service and carton scope equivalent?

Use a representative assembly trial rather than a presumed labour rate. If the rigid and paperboard concepts use different vial counts, resize both around the same product brief before treating the quotations as alternatives. The displayed images are design references, not existing stock or a price promise.
Sources
1. ISTA: packaged-product test procedure families, accessed 18 November 2026.

imageAlt: AI generated illustrative shaped packaging concept
title: How to Specify a Radial Insert for a Hinged Hexagonal Gift Box
seoTitle: Hinged Hexagonal Box Radial Insert Fit | MTT
summary: Check the largest wrapped item against the narrow end of each radial compartment. On a loaded sample, check finger access and clearance under the hinged lid.
intro: You have selected a six-sided presentation box and want customers to see a ring of individually presented pieces when they lift the cover. The next decision is the insert, not the exterior print: the layout must accommodate the largest actual wrapped item, leave a way to remove it and remain clear of the lid when the box closes. Treat the reference drawing as a starting shape; approve the final number and position of recesses against a physical sample.
cta: Share your product dimensions, desired structure and quantity. MTT reviews custom packaging briefs from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Start with the object, including its wrapping

Measure the maximum length, width and thickness of each packed item. Include the seam or twist of an individual wrapper, any label, and the way the item will enter its recess. For an assortment, compare every shape in the range rather than assuming that pieces with equal net weight have equal envelopes. Provide the supplier with a position map and an extra set of actual packed pieces for fitting.

Radial compartments converge toward the center. That creates a narrow tip even when the outside edge looks generous. Ask for a section and plan showing the usable area of each recess, the bridge between adjacent recesses and the room required for fingers to grip the item. A recess that fits an item when pushed straight down may make it hard to lift out again.
Separate product retention from insert retention

The insert has to locate the items, while the box has to locate the insert. These are separate questions. Confirm whether the insert rests on the base, has a supporting layer beneath it or needs a finger notch to be removed. Ensure the insert does not ride into the hinge when the lid closes. Paperboard, wrapped board or other proposed supports should be reviewed with the actual item and finish; the reference image does not establish a material or thickness.

For a food gift, identify whether the pieces are individually wrapped and whether any packaging surface contacts food. Ask the appropriate supplier to document the material for the intended contact and destination; do not assume a decorative gift box or an unverified material is suitable for direct contact.
Test the opening sequence

Place the full assortment in a representative sample, close the lid and reopen it in the way a customer would. Record whether the lid clears the product, the cover aligns with the base, and each item can be lifted out without disturbing its neighbours. If the closing system includes magnets, tabs or ribbons, verify their location on the sample rather than assuming they are present in the reference. Check the complete shipping pack for the intended distribution route; ISTA describes different packaged-product procedure families.

Brief for MTT: provide the largest wrapped item, item count and position map, target dimensions, color and logo artwork, quantity per design and shipping destination. Custom briefs start at 1,000 boxes per design; construction and fit are confirmed through sampling.
Explore the structure
Review the packaging concept and send the actual contents and specification for a sample review. Images illustrate concepts, not completed projects.

imageAlt: AI generated illustrative shaped packaging concept
title: Half-Moon Gift Box: How to Check a Separate Lid and Curved Wall
seoTitle: Half-Moon Gift Box Lid and Curved Wall | MTT
summary: Check how the lift-off lid seats along both the curved wall and the straight edge. Load the intended product and check that the lid lifts without binding.
intro: A half-moon box is defined by two matching semicircular pieces: a base and a separate lift-off cover. Begin with the product envelope and the way the buyer will remove the lid. A visually attractive curve does not by itself establish the internal space, lid fit or whether a curved wall can be wrapped neatly in the selected paper.
cta: Share your product dimensions, desired structure and quantity. MTT reviews custom packaging briefs from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Specify the shape in the right view

Supply a front or plan view showing the straight edge and curve, then a side view showing box depth and cover height. Identify which dimensions describe the inside cavity and which describe the assembled outside. If an object or tray must fit, include its maximum envelope and the intended orientation. Do not substitute a circular diameter for a measured internal opening without checking board thickness, wrapping and the actual construction.

The buyer may want the finished box to stand on its flat edge for display. If so, state that requirement explicitly and evaluate stability with the actual contents, lid and display surface. A picture is not evidence that a loaded set will stand safely.
Review curve, wrap and lid together

Ask the manufacturer how the selected wall and wrap will be formed along the curve, where the seam is expected and how the two ends meet the straight section. The cover and base must follow compatible curves without preventing normal removal. Thick or heavily textured wrap can change the fit and the appearance at the curved edge; inspect the proposed material in a production-representative sample before approving artwork.

Printed logos and foil require their own layout review. A mark placed across a curved transition may not read like a flat-screen mockup. Show the logo placement on an assembled sample, agree an orientation and inspect it in the viewing direction customers will use.
Make the sample a decision tool

Test the empty lid first, then repeat with the actual insert and product. Record where the user grips the cover, whether the contents touch its interior and whether the base remains supported while the lid is removed. Review multiple samples when available and agree acceptance criteria with the supplier; no single lid clearance is appropriate for every board, wrap and size.

For delivery, specify whether covers and bases ship assembled, nested or separately, and how they are protected from abrasion. Use the loaded outer pack when assessing the appropriate transport-test plan. Quote the insert, finishes, tooling, samples and freight separately where applicable.

Brief for MTT: share a sketch, product measurements, planned standing or lying orientation, visual references, quantity and destination. Custom packaging starts at 1,000 pieces per design. The color images are concepts; final colors, branding and construction are developed to the customer's requirements.
Explore the structure
Review the packaging concept and send the actual contents and specification for a sample review. Images illustrate concepts, not completed projects.

imageAlt: AI generated illustrative shaped packaging concept
title: Comparing Quotes for Shaped Rigid Boxes: Hinged Hexagon vs Half-Moon Lid
seoTitle: Shaped Rigid Box Quote Comparison | MTT
summary: Compare shaped gift box quotes using the same insert layout, artwork, sample scope and delivery terms. Ask each supplier to itemise tooling and packing costs.
intro: When two suppliers quote a shaped gift box, the lower price may describe a different package. A hinged six-sided box with a radial insert and a separate-lid half-moon box are different assemblies. Compare each quote against a common brief and an agreed sample, then separate one-time costs from per-piece costs before deciding.
cta: Share your product dimensions, desired structure and quantity. MTT reviews custom packaging briefs from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Make the two structures explicit

For the hinged format, identify the cover-to-base connection, closing method if any, insert layout and the number of compartments. For the half-moon format, identify the separate lid, curved wall, straight edge and the intended presentation orientation. Give inside and outside dimensions separately and identify the exact object or protective wrapping included in the fit. Ask each supplier to identify assumptions on its quote.

A visual reference can communicate shape, color and mood. It cannot confirm board grade, hinge durability, compartment count, tested load or material certifications. Treat the image as a concept until a structural drawing and representative physical sample have been reviewed.
Compare the same commercial scope

Ask for separate lines for the outer assembly, insert and each optional accessory, together with printing, logo finishes, tooling and sample charges. Specify the total quantity and the number of different artworks or sizes. A change in art versions or packing method can change setup and handling; do not assume a single unit price applies across every configuration.

Request the shipping basis, destination, packing arrangement and the dimensions and weight of the packed master carton when available. Mark preliminary freight figures as estimates and confirm trade terms and what is included before comparing them. Flat or curved shapes can pack differently even when the finished presentation areas appear similar.
Use sampling to close the gaps

Agree which revision of the drawing and artwork each sample represents. Place the actual contents and accessories in the sample, check the opening and closing sequence, and record the dimensions and visible finish against the brief. Inspect the curved wrap, polygon corners or hinged area as appropriate to the structure. Check the fully packed set using a test plan suited to its actual distribution route; a supplier's sample approval is not a substitute for an agreed transport test.

Where a component is made from folding paperboard, the board and crease must be assessed together. Holmen Iggesund's converting guidance describes how crease design and material properties affect folding; it does not certify an individual finished rigid box.

Brief for MTT: send the reference shape, product list and dimensions, target quantity per design, logo file, proposed material or finish, optional accessories and destination. MTT can review custom briefs from 1,000 pieces per design; all product fit and material choices remain subject to sample approval.
Explore the structure
Review the packaging concept and send the actual contents and specification for a sample review. Images illustrate concepts, not completed projects.

imageAlt: Illustrative custom packaging concept, not a manufactured sample
title: Hinged Lid and Bottom Drawer Gift Box: A Buyer’s Sample Review
seoTitle: Hinged Lid and Bottom Drawer Gift Box: A Buyer’s Sample Review | MTT
summary: The top compartment and the bottom drawer must work as one loaded structure. Decide how the contents are supported, then check the hinged lid, separation panel and drawer together. A box that opens smoothly while empty may behave differently once the intended items and packing materials are added.
intro: The top compartment and the bottom drawer must work as one loaded structure. Decide how the contents are supported, then check the hinged lid, separation panel and drawer together. A box that opens smoothly while empty may behave differently once the intended items and packing materials are added.
cta: Share product dimensions, quantities by design, artwork, destination and packing plan. MTT can review custom packaging projects from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Start with the load path, not the decoration

Imagine receiving a beautiful two-level sample: the lid opens cleanly, but as you pull the filled drawer, the upper section shifts or the pull tab becomes hard to reach. The issue may be the interaction of components rather than the pull itself. This is an illustrative purchasing scenario, not a reported MTT project.

List every item, its maximum dimensions, filled weight, fragile features and placement. Establish which surfaces can carry load. Mark what is fixed to the upper compartment, what sits in the drawer and how the intermediate panel is supported. Avoid assuming the slot pattern shown in a visual fits your product.
Check the lid and drawer as a complete assembly

Review the lid open and closed, first without contents and then with the proposed upper insert, products, leaflet and tissue. Where a ribbon acts as a lid stay, note its attachment points, resting position and whether it touches the contents. Confirm the opening angle needed for access without treating a rendering as proof of hinge or stay strength.

With the lid closed, slide the empty drawer; repeat with the complete lower set. Look for front-to-front alignment, contact or scraping, unwanted movement and a pull that is easy to grasp. If resistance changes only after loading, investigate the insert, bottom support and local deformation before changing all drawer dimensions. The existing drawer-clearance guide covers sleeve friction and pull placement.
Agree how the set is packed and reviewed

Write the sequence: erect the box, fit the upper panel, position each product, load the lower drawer, insert the drawer and close the lid. Record whether products arrive at one packing location and whether the drawer must remain removable. Check finger access without lifting fragile parts by a cap or decoration.

A sample record should identify the drawing revision, actual contents, all included accessories, where friction appears and the change requested. Ask for a revised physical sample when structural changes affect another component. Holmen notes that material and conversion settings affect paperboard behaviour; a board or crease setting cannot be transferred blindly from another job.[1]
Ask for a comparable quotation

Request separate lines for box shell, upper support, drawer insert, example and production artwork, sampling, tooling and outer shipping pack. State the quantity for each artwork version and destination. Compare like-for-like components before deciding whether a lower unit price really reflects the same set.

Review the two-tier concept with your product samples. MTT can review structural options and coordinate samples for custom projects from 1,000 pieces per design; the pictured logo, colours and finish are examples.
Decision table: record the next action

Buyer decision record
Review pointWhat may go wrongNext decision
Upper compartmentLoaded panel presses the lid or ribbonCheck tallest fitted product and layer stack before moving the panel.
Lower drawerDrawer moves empty but binds when filledReview base support, loaded insert and contact location before changing clearance.
Packing sequenceUpper panel prevents drawer or item loadingTrial the full order with the intended packer and keep the revision.
Release decisionOne component changed after approvalRecheck affected lid, drawer and insert interactions on the revised sample.

Use this as a discussion framework, not as a claim that the pictured concept has been manufactured or passed a test. Keep the actual sample, contents and revision together when comparing changes.
Sources
1. Primary technical reference, accessed 19 November 2026.

imageAlt: Illustrative custom packaging concept, not a manufactured sample
title: Upright Double-Door Gift Box: Support Frame and Door Clearance
seoTitle: Upright Double-Door Gift Box: Support Frame and Door Clearance | MTT
summary: An upright frame can present a product between two opening doors, but a rectangular recess alone does not define how the item is held. Determine support points, removal direction and the path of both doors using the actual product and the proposed packing sequence.
intro: An upright frame can present a product between two opening doors, but a rectangular recess alone does not define how the item is held. Determine support points, removal direction and the path of both doors using the actual product and the proposed packing sequence.
cta: Share product dimensions, quantities by design, artwork, destination and packing plan. MTT can review custom packaging projects from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Specify what the frame supports

Imagine a gift set whose product looks centered in the artwork, but its cap projects beyond the frame and catches a door as it closes. The buyer needs a side section through the loaded assembly, not just a front elevation. This is an illustrative scenario, not a completed MTT case.

Measure the complete filled primary pack, including cap, decoration, protrusions and protective sleeve. Identify stable support surfaces and fragile surfaces that must not be compressed. State whether the item stands on its base, rests in a shaped insert or needs a separate retainer. Confirm the actual mechanism by sample; a rendered frame does not show its load capacity.
Review two doors, one product and the base together

Draw the door travel and inspect the central meeting edge. Check that the supported product, any ribbon and the insert do not intersect the path when each door closes separately and when both close together. Confirm alignment and access without assuming that either magnets or a particular fastening are included.

The upright plinth and intended display position affect stability. Ask the supplier to review the filled unit on its intended surface and during the proposed packing operation; a display check is not a transport qualification. If the product sits high or is heavy, review the base and outer pack with the real load.
Plan removal without pulling on a fragile part

Decide where the recipient can grip the item and what is removed first. A finger recess, removable tray or retainer may be appropriate, but each changes presentation and tooling. Test the chosen solution with the actual primary pack, with any protective sleeve in place. Check contact marks and whether the support stays in position when the item is lifted.

Document the product orientation, support locations, open-door footprint, packing orientation and sample revision. If a second product size is added, recheck both door travel and support; the same external box can conceal a different interference.
Request an itemised solution

Discuss the upright double-door concept, its frame and a separate shipping pack. FedEx lists different packaged-product distribution tests; select the relevant method and acceptance criteria with the responsible laboratory or carrier rather than claiming a render has passed.[1]

Send MTT finished product drawings or samples, filled weights, quantity per design, destination, intended retail or parcel route, and logo artwork. Custom concepts start at 1,000 pieces per design; the sample establishes feasible materials, structure and finish.
Decision table: record the next action

Buyer decision record
Review pointWhat may go wrongNext decision

title: Ribbon Lid Stays for Hinged Gift Boxes: What to Check on a Sample
seoTitle: Ribbon Lid Stay: Gift Box Sample Checks | MTT
summary: A lid stay affects the opening path, presentation and packing operation. Decide the desired access, attachment position and folding path, then review the loaded box with the actual ribbon and lid materials. The correct arrangement depends on the lid and use; a picture is not a tested specification.
intro: A lid stay affects the opening path, presentation and packing operation. Decide the desired access, attachment position and folding path, then review the loaded box with the actual ribbon and lid materials. The correct arrangement depends on the lid and use; a picture is not a tested specification.
cta: Share product dimensions, quantities by design, artwork, destination and packing plan. MTT can review custom packaging projects from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Define what the ribbon is expected to do

A buyer can receive a sample that looks correct in a photograph but leaves the ribbon resting across the insert when closed. Another layout may open well on a display table but require a packer to hold the lid during loading. Treat these as different review questions; they are illustrative scenarios.

Record the intended opening, position of the box when used, access required above the contents and whether the ribbon is decorative or also intended to limit travel. Ask how the lid is supported during packing. Do not assume a single stay location, ribbon length or opening angle is appropriate for every lid.
Inspect attachment and folding paths

On the proposed sample, identify both attachment positions and whether they interfere with the wrap, hinge or insert. Open and close by the normal user path and observe where the ribbon folds. Check for trapping at the hinge, rubbing on a decorated surface or interference with a product.

Review with lid, insert, tissue and contents together. A ribbon that clears an empty box may sit against a tall cap after loading. If a change to the lid or liner shifts the attachment, mark the new drawing revision and repeat the fit review.
Agree acceptance rather than promise a universal life

The project team should define the handling sequence and any durability requirements with the supplier or test laboratory. Record the sample build, lid material, attachment method and observed results. Do not advertise a cycle count or safe load until a suitable documented test supports it.

Holmen explains that conversion settings depend on the specific board and tool configuration; while a wrapped rigid-box hinge is a different construction, this supports using an appropriate physical sample rather than a universal fold setting.[1]
Include the stay in the quote and packing brief

Request a description of ribbon material, colour, attachment, lid/liner construction, sample and tooling scope, and whether the assembly arrives ready to fill. Check whether the stay is included in all compared quotations.

See the hinged lid and drawer concept and send lid dimensions, contents, target opening use and artwork. MTT can discuss a custom sample from 1,000 pieces per design.

title: Two-Level Gift Box Pack-Out: Product Order and Artwork Version Control
seoTitle: Two-Level Gift Box Pack-Out Planning | MTT
summary: A two-level presentation box needs a loading map as well as a structural drawing. Identify which component goes in each level, which version it carries, and the order in which a packer can load and close the set without disturbing an earlier layer.
intro: A two-level presentation box needs a loading map as well as a structural drawing. Identify which component goes in each level, which version it carries, and the order in which a packer can load and close the set without disturbing an earlier layer.
cta: Share product dimensions, quantities by design, artwork, destination and packing plan. MTT can review custom packaging projects from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Map the set before approving the insert

Consider an illustrative set with a printed card on the upper layer and a long accessory in the drawer. Both components fit individually, yet the drawer cannot be loaded after the upper panel is fixed. The question is not only cavity size: the sequence and access must be designed together.

Create a list of all primary packs, caps, sleeves, instruction cards and optional accessories. Assign each a level, orientation and version. Provide maximum dimensions and filled weights, and specify whether the items arrive individually wrapped. Avoid claiming that a generic slotted panel suits every item.
Use a numbered physical loading trial

On the sample, number each position and write the insertion order. Check whether the drawer is loaded outside the cabinet, whether the top insert is fixed or removable, and which item blocks access to the next. Record who supplies and inserts cards or tissue.

Try the full set with real product samples in the intended orientation. Close the lid and drawer, then reopen them as the recipient would. Check that the pull tab is reachable and that removing one item does not dislodge another. Compare this with the general PR-kit pack-out checklist without assuming that a different layout can be copied.
Keep artwork and component versions linked

Use a single revision table linking box artwork, insert orientation, card language, product variant and quantity. When a variant changes, identify the affected cavity, printed component and packing instructions. Ask the supplier and packing partner to agree the same reference before production.

A colour or coating change can alter how surfaces behave; Holmen notes that ink and varnish influence friction and rub. Confirm the actual material and finishing combination in a sample, and do not infer a quantitative friction value from this general guidance.[1]
Turn the map into a supplier brief

Share the numbered list, photographs, product drawings, packing location, artwork revision and destination. Ask for a sample and a price breakdown for shell, inserts, cards, optional accessories and freight. Define who approves the final loaded sample.

title: Double-Door Presentation Box: Sample Approval Checklist
seoTitle: Double-Door Presentation Box: Sample Approval Checklist | MTT
summary: A useful approval record describes what was actually checked: the door edges, loaded insert, removal, appearance and complete closed assembly. It should also identify the sample revision and any remaining transport or production checks, rather than turning a visual approval into a performance claim.
intro: A useful approval record describes what was actually checked: the door edges, loaded insert, removal, appearance and complete closed assembly. It should also identify the sample revision and any remaining transport or production checks, rather than turning a visual approval into a performance claim.
cta: Share product dimensions, quantities by design, artwork, destination and packing plan. MTT can review custom packaging projects from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Separate visual approval from functional review

Imagine approving a print colour while the door-to-door gap has not yet been reviewed with the final insert. Those are different decisions. Use a short approval record that distinguishes the printed artwork, the assembled empty box and the filled sample. This is an illustrative example, not a project outcome.

Record the version of each part: left and right doors, wrap, plinth, frame, insert and primary product. List the colours and finishes as sample references; a digital image cannot establish exact colour or foil appearance.
Check movement and contact in a consistent order

Place the box in its intended position, open each door and inspect the hinge area and meeting edge. Load the final representative product and insert, then close each door and both together. Look for a protruding product, interference, uneven contact and any abrasion observed during normal operation.

If a door catches, identify the first point of contact before requesting a larger box. A shifted insert, excess product projection, folded tissue or alignment may be responsible. Note the actual finding and revise the relevant component. Do not set a universal door gap or force from a photograph.
Review product access and handoff

Ask a person unfamiliar with the sample to find where to grip the product. Check that the supporting frame remains stable and that removal does not pull on a cap or decorated edge. Record the intended packing order and how doors are protected until the recipient opens the box.

For a filled sample moving through a carrier network, define the outer carton, cushioning, route and acceptance criteria separately. FedEx lists distribution and material tests; selection and results require a specific documented test with the agreed pack.[1] A display sample is not evidence of passing such a test.
Issue a controlled approval and quote request

List accepted characteristics, deviations, photographs, product versions and unresolved checks. Request an updated sample when a material, position or closure change may affect function. Agree the point at which the artwork and construction are frozen.

title: How to Keep the Right Nail Wrap Visible Through a Carton Window
seoTitle: How to Keep the Right Nail Wrap Visible Through a Carton Window | MTT
intro: Before you approve the window die, move the smallest artwork motif to both limits of the carrier pocket. The window has to show the intended design even when the sheet shifts. Record the aperture, sheet position and pocket stops separately so a later artwork change does not quietly undo the fit.
summary: Before you approve the window die, move the smallest artwork motif to both limits of the carrier pocket.
imageAlt: Illustrative nail wrap envelope carton window
sections: Start with the motif the shopper must see

Lay the actual sealed sheet behind an opaque card with a trial opening. Mark the part a shopper needs to recognise: shade, pattern scale or finish. A centred window can still show half of two different wraps. Repeat with the busiest and sparsest designs, keeping the same outer carton.
Trace the movement envelope

With the sample closed, push the carrier gently left, right, up and down. Trace the visible area at each extreme on a spare sheet. The overlap is the dependable display area for that sample. If the desired motif falls outside it, try a folded stop before enlarging the cutout. A larger window also leaves less board at its corners.
Separate visibility from product protection

An open aperture exposes the primary pack to handling. Review whether the actual wrap already arrives sealed. If the brand requests a window patch, ask for a patched sample and check glare, adhesive visibility and sheet insertion. Keep the primary seal intact throughout the review.
Give the converter two controlled files

Send the carrier print file and carton dieline at the same scale, identify the front face and loading direction, and photograph both travel limits. Ask for separate prices for one common die and any shade-specific changes. Approve the loaded unit under the lighting used for shelf review.

Review the windowed nail wrap envelope alongside your actual components. See the cosmetic packaging specification guide for the dimensions and artwork needed for a quotation.

title: Can Two Airless Pump Sizes Share One Carton Insert?
seoTitle: Can Two Airless Pump Sizes Share One Carton Insert? | MTT
intro: Compare the largest pump body, the smallest body and the heaviest filled pair before committing to one insert. The tallest pair governs closed headroom, while the narrowest bottle may govern retention. A common outer carton with two insert variants can be worth quoting when one pocket cannot meet both conditions.
summary: Compare the largest pump body, the smallest body and the heaviest filled pair before committing to one insert.
imageAlt: Illustrative folded paperboard cradle for two pump bottles
sections: Build a variant matrix from finished packs

Make one row per bottle revision. Record capped height, body width at the proposed support, filled mass and any label seam. Include the removable overcap. Two nominally identical fills can use different pump heads. Ask purchasing to flag which combinations may actually be sold together.
Test the opposing limits

Place the shortest narrow bottle beside the tallest wide one. Tilt the assembled presentation pack as a handling check and observe where the narrow bottle moves first. Then close the lid over the tall bottle with a removable contact witness above the cap. Inspect for compression without actuating the pump. These observations guide fit changes and do not qualify a parcel pack.
Price the insert decision separately

If widening the pocket releases the narrow bottle, compare a replaceable folded collar with a dedicated insert. The collar adds a packing operation and another part to control. A dedicated insert adds a second item to inventory. Quote the same total quantity split by variant and ask how a packer will distinguish the two.
Approve a loading instruction

Photograph both SKUs correctly seated, with the lid open and closed. Mark which surface supports the bottle and which area stays clear. Record the insert revision beside the bottle revision. Recheck the retained sample when the pump supplier changes its closure.

title: Quoting a Skincare Kit When Only Empty Containers Are Available
seoTitle: Quoting a Skincare Kit When Only Empty Containers Are Available | MTT
intro: An empty jar can establish an outline, but it cannot show how far a loaded insert will deflect. Ask for a provisional quotation using documented dimensions and an explicit mass assumption. Reserve structural approval until the supplier can review the filled retail units in the proposed presentation and shipping packs.
summary: An empty jar can establish an outline, but it cannot show how far a loaded insert will deflect.
imageAlt: Concept gift carton loaded with two capped bottles
sections: Keep geometry and loading on separate lines

Use the empty container to locate the body, cap and decoration. List the expected gross mass of each filled, closed SKU separately. A nominal volume is insufficient to calculate gross mass without the fill density and the container mass. A buyer with finished stock can weigh one complete unit and identify exactly which revision was weighed.
Use a surrogate for a limited question

For an early layout discussion, identify a dummy as a dummy. Matching total weight at the bottom of a bottle can hide a tendency to tilt if the real mass sits higher. Keep unknowns on the sample label. Use the actual primary pack before accepting support, surface contact or customer removal.
Ask what would change the quote

Ask the supplier to separate the outer shell, insert construction, sample charge and packing operation. If base reinforcement or a second support level is provisional, mark it on the quote. This lets procurement compare two quotes without assuming that both include the same reinforcement.
Define the release point

Before ordering, record the actual loaded weight, photos of the closed kit and the approved insert revision. If the loaded jar visibly depresses its platform, change the load path and repeat the check with the adjacent bottles installed. Record shipping-pack approval separately from presentation approval.

title: One Carton for Several Nail Wrap Shades: How to Prevent Packing Mix-Ups
seoTitle: Nail Wrap Shade Assortments: Prevent Packing Mix-Ups | MTT
intro: A shared printed carton reduces artwork versions only if the packer and the customer can both identify the enclosed shade. Decide which identifier remains on the primary pack, which belongs on the outer carton and when the match is checked. Test the process with the two shades that are easiest to confuse.
summary: A shared printed carton reduces artwork versions only if the packer and the customer can both identify the enclosed shade.
imageAlt: Concept envelope beside its nail wrap sheet
sections: Simulate one line change

Place the previous shade and the next shade side by side with their actual carrier cards. Pack one of each in the proposed envelope. Ask someone who did not prepare them to identify both using the closed cartons. Similar artwork can make a window a weak identifier even when the colour appears clear in a design file.
Compare common and dedicated print

A common shell plus a variable label lets the same blank serve several shades. It introduces a label selection step. A dedicated printed shell removes that step but creates more packaging inventory. Ask for costs at the actual quantity per shade and identify which packaging remains usable if one shade is discontinued.
Set a reading position

Choose an area visible after folding and away from the flap edge. If the label carries a retail barcode, have the brand supply the approved code for that exact saleable item and verify it on the finished pack. A successful phone scan alone does not prove retail print quality.
Write the sign-off in packing order

Record the shade reference, carrier ID, carton or label revision and finished photograph for the first accepted pack of each changeover. Build a deliberate mismatch into the trial and confirm where it is caught. Keep customer-facing shade naming identical across the pack and order specification.

title: How to Locate Label Scuffing in a Skincare Gift Kit Sample
seoTitle: How to Locate Label Scuffing in a Skincare Gift Kit Sample | MTT
intro: When a decorated bottle picks up a mark, identify the first operation that produces it. Loading, closing, carrying and removal can each create contact at a different point. Compare photographs after each operation before changing the finish or widening every cavity in the insert.
summary: When a decorated bottle picks up a mark, identify the first operation that produces it.
sections: Mark the contact map

Use a sacrificial decorated sample and photograph the clean bottle under fixed light. Note label edges, raised foil and seams relative to the cradle. Load it once and remove it along the intended grip path. Check both the bottle and the corresponding paper edge for residue.
Change one movement at a time

Repeat with a fresh sample for lid closure, then for handling the complete closed kit. A line that appears on loading directs attention to the lead-in edge. A broad rub patch that appears only after movement calls for checking retention and side play. These are hypotheses to confirm on another sample.
Compare two fixes with different costs

Changing the loading angle or moving a support below a decorated band may preserve the existing surface material. A softer contact layer may protect a sensitive label but adds thickness that can tighten the pocket. Check the narrowest opening and repeat removal before approving the revised lining.
Agree what counts as a defect

Record lighting, viewing angle, reference photographs and the specific visible face that matters. Give the packer a photo of the approved loading orientation. If parcel transport is part of the brief, send the complete shipper for an agreed assessment; a clean hand-loaded presentation sample answers only the handling question.
